title: TX SB1964: Relating to the regulation and use of artificial intelligence systems and the management of data by governmental entities.

obligations: The department shall collect from each state agency information on the status and condition of the agency's information technology infrastructure, including an inventory of artificial intelligence systems and heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.068(b)).

A state agency's information resources review must include an inventory and identification of artificial intelligence systems and heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems deployed by the agency, an evaluation of the purpose of and risk mitigation measures for each system, an analysis of each system's support of the agency's strategic plan, and confirmation of compliance with state statutes, rules, and standards relating to information resources and artificial intelligence systems, including the code of ethics and minimum standards (Sec. 2054.0965(b)(6)-(7)).
Local governments shall complete a review of the deployment and use of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems and, on request, provide the review to the department (Sec. 2054.0965(c)).

A state agency with 150 or fewer full-time employees may designate a full-time employee to serve as a data management officer or enter into an agreement with one or more state agencies to jointly employ a data management officer if approved by the department (Sec. 2054.137(a-1)).

The data management officer for a state agency shall annually post on the Texas Open Data Portal at least three high value data sets, excluding information that is confidential or protected from disclosure under state or federal law (Sec. 2054.137(c)).

The department by rule shall establish an artificial intelligence system code of ethics for use by state agencies and local governments that procure, develop, deploy, or use artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.702(a)).

The code of ethics must include guidance aligning with the NIST AI RMF 1.0 and addressing human oversight and control, fairness and accuracy, transparency including consumer disclosures, data privacy and security, public and internal redress including accountability and liability, and the frequency of evaluations and documentation of improvements (Sec. 2054.702(b)).
State agencies and local governments shall adopt the code of ethics (Sec. 2054.702(c)).

The department by rule shall develop minimum risk management and governance standards for the development, procurement, deployment, and use of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems by a state agency or local government (Sec. 2054.703(a)).

The minimum standards must be consistent with the NIST AI RMF 1.0 and include accountability measures, required assessment and documentation of known security risks, performance metrics, and transparency measures before deploying and at material changes, resources for local governments, and guidelines for risk management frameworks, acceptable use policies, employee training, and contractual vendor risk management (Sec. 2054.703(b)).
State agencies and local governments shall adopt the minimum standards (Sec. 2054.703(c)).

The department shall develop educational materials on artificial intelligence systems, training materials for state and local government employees and the general public, make training materials available on its public Internet website, and host statewide forums and training sessions (Sec. 2054.704(a)-(c)).

The public sector artificial intelligence systems advisory board shall obtain and disseminate information, facilitate shared resources, consult with the department, identify opportunities for state agencies to implement artificial intelligence systems and streamline procurement, and recommend elimination of rules that restrict innovation (Sec. 2054.705(b)).

The department shall establish and administer a sandbox program to support eligible entities in contracting with vendors for research, development, training, testing, and other predeployment activities related to artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.706(b)).

The department shall create an application process for vendors that includes a detailed description of the artificial intelligence system and intended use, a risk assessment addressing potential impacts on the public, and a plan for mitigating adverse consequences discovered during testing (Sec. 2054.706(c)).

A vendor participating in the sandbox program shall, with oversight by the department, provide eligible entities with secure access to an artificial intelligence system used in the program (Sec. 2054.706(d)).
The department shall provide detailed guidelines regarding the exemption from compliance with otherwise applicable regulations provided by the program (Sec. 2054.706(e)).

Eligible entities and vendors shall submit quarterly reports to the department including performance measures, risk mitigation strategies, feedback on program effectiveness and efficiency, and any additional information the department requests (Sec. 2054.706(f)).
The department shall produce an annual report and submit it to the legislature by November 30 of each even numbered year summarizing participants, outcomes, and recommendations (Sec. 2054.706(g)).

A state agency that procures, develops, deploys, or uses a public facing artificial intelligence system shall provide clear disclosure of interaction with the system to the public as provided by the code of ethics (Sec. 2054.707).

A state agency that deploys or uses a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system or a vendor that contracts with a state agency for the deployment or use of such a system shall conduct a system assessment outlining risks of unlawful harm, system limitations, and information governance practices (Sec. 2054.708(a)).
The state agency or vendor shall make a copy of the assessment available to the department on request (Sec. 2054.708(b)).

The department shall take actions necessary to ensure the confidentiality of information submitted under the impact assessment section, including restricting access to only authorized personnel and implementing physical, electronic, and procedural protections (Sec. 2054.708(d)).

If a state agency or vendor becomes aware of a violation of Subchapter S, the agency or vendor shall report the violation to the department, if applicable, and the attorney general (Sec. 2054.709(a)).
The attorney general shall review a report or complaint and determine whether to bring an action to enjoin a violation (Sec. 2054.709(b)).
If the attorney general determines that a vendor violated Subchapter S, the attorney general shall provide the vendor with a written notice of the violation (Sec. 2054.709(c)).

If a vendor fails to respond or cure the violation within 31 days after receiving the written notice, the state agency shall provide the vendor with a notice of intent to void the contract (Sec. 2054.709(d)).
The attorney general shall establish a web page in collaboration with the department allowing a person to report complaints relating to artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.710(a)).
A complaint submitted on the web page must be distributed to the department (Sec. 2054.710(b)).
The attorney general shall post information educating persons about risks and benefits of artificial intelligence systems and explaining a person's rights (Sec. 2054.710(d)).
The attorney general shall submit a report to the legislature by November 30 of each even numbered year summarizing complaints, resolutions, and enforcement actions (Sec. 2054.710(f)).

Each state agency and local government deploying or using an artificial intelligence system that is public facing or that is a controlling factor in a consequential decision shall include a standardized notice on all related applications, Internet websites, and public computer systems (Sec. 2054.711(a)).

The department shall develop a form for the standardized notice that includes general information about the system and data sources and measures taken to maintain compliance with information privacy laws and ethics standards (Sec. 2054.711(b)).

The department shall coordinate activities under Subchapter S and any other law relating to artificial intelligence systems to ensure efficient implementation and streamline resources (Sec. 2054.712).
The department shall adopt rules to implement Subchapter S (Sec. 2054.713).

As soon as practicable after the effective date, the Department of Information Resources shall adopt rules necessary to implement Subchapter S and develop the outreach program and form required by Sections 2054.704 and 2054.711 (Sec. 6(a)).
As soon as practicable after the effective date, the office of the attorney general shall establish the web page required by Section 2054.710 (Sec. 6(b)).
prohibitions: The high value data sets posted by a data management officer may not include information that is confidential or protected from disclosure under state or federal law (Sec. 2054.137(c)).

An impact assessment conducted under Section 2054.708 is confidential and not subject to disclosure under Chapter 552; the state agency or department may redact or withhold information as confidential under Chapter 552 without requesting a decision from the attorney general (Sec. 2054.708(c)).
The department shall restrict access to submitted impact assessment information to only authorized personnel (Sec. 2054.708(d)).
Advisory board members are not entitled to compensation or reimbursement of expenses for service on the advisory board (Sec. 2054.705(f)).
reading.what_it_does: Texas SB 1964 directs the Department of Information Resources to establish an artificial intelligence code of ethics, minimum risk management standards for heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems, educational outreach, an advisory board, a sandbox program, disclosure and impact assessment requirements, and enforcement mechanisms. It applies to state agencies, local governments, and vendors contracting with state agencies for artificial intelligence deployment or use. The Act takes effect September 1, 2025.
key_definitions: Artificial intelligence system: a machine based system that for explicit or implicit objectives infers from provided information a method to generate outputs, such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions, to influence a physical or virtual environment with varying levels of autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment (Sec. 2054.003(1-a)).
Consequential decision: a decision that has a material legal or similarly significant effect on the provision, denial, or conditions of a person's access to a government service (Sec. 2054.003(2-b)).
Controlling factor: a factor that is the principal basis for making a consequential decision or capable of altering the outcome of a consequential decision (Sec. 2054.003(2-c)).

Heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system: an artificial intelligence system specifically intended to autonomously make, or be a controlling factor in making, a consequential decision; does not include an artificial intelligence system intended to perform a narrow procedural task, improve the result of a previously completed human activity, perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant to a consequential decision, or detect decision making patterns or deviations from previous decision making patterns (Sec. 2054.003(6-a)).

Principal basis: the use of an output produced by a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system to make a decision without human review, oversight, involvement, or intervention, or without meaningful consideration by a human (Sec. 2054.003(11)).

Unlawful harm: any condition in which the use of an artificial intelligence system results in a consequential decision that causes harm to an individual who is a member of a state or federally protected class in violation of law; does not include a developer's or deployer's offer, license, or use of a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system for the sole purpose of testing the system before deployment to identify, mitigate, or otherwise ensure compliance with state and federal law (Sec. 2054.701).
Eligible entity: an eligible customer under Section 2054.0525 (Sec. 2054.706(a)(1)).

Program: the program established by Section 2054.706 designed to allow temporary testing of an artificial intelligence system in a controlled, limited manner without requiring full compliance with otherwise applicable regulations (Sec. 2054.706(a)(2)).
Vendor: a person registered with the department as a contractor to provide commodity items under Section 2157.068 (Sec. 2054.706(a)(3)).
compliance_steps: Identify whether any artificial intelligence systems are heightened scrutiny, public facing, or controlling factors in consequential decisions (Sec. 2054.003, Sec. 2054.707, Sec. 2054.711).

Inventory all artificial intelligence systems and heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems in information technology infrastructure reports and information resources reviews (Sec. 2054.068(b), Sec. 2054.0965(b)(6)).
Adopt the department's artificial intelligence code of ethics and minimum risk management standards once rules are adopted (Sec. 2054.702(c), Sec. 2054.703(c)).
For public facing artificial intelligence systems, provide clear disclosure of interaction unless a reasonable person would know (Sec. 2054.707).

For public facing or controlling factor artificial intelligence systems, include the department's standardized notice on all related applications, Internet websites, and public computer systems (Sec. 2054.711(a)-(b)).

For heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems, conduct a system assessment outlining risks of unlawful harm, system limitations, and information governance practices, and make it available to the department on request while keeping it confidential (Sec. 2054.708).
If a vendor, implement risk management frameworks as contractually required, participate in the sandbox program if applicable, and submit quarterly reports (Sec. 2054.703(b)(4)(B), Sec. 2054.706).
Report any known violation of Subchapter S to the department and attorney general; respond to written notices and cure violations within 31 days to avoid contract voiding (Sec. 2054.709).
Local governments complete a review of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence deployment and provide it to the department on request (Sec. 2054.0965(c)).

For state agencies, designate or jointly employ a data management officer if 150 or fewer employees, and ensure the data management officer posts high value data sets excluding confidential information (Sec. 2054.137).

Monitor department rules, code of ethics, minimum standards, educational materials, and the attorney general's complaint web page; comply with enforcement actions (Sec. 2054.702, Sec. 2054.703, Sec. 2054.704, Sec. 2054.710, Sec. 2054.713).

What it does

Texas SB 1964 directs the Department of Information Resources to establish an artificial intelligence code of ethics, minimum risk management standards for heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems, educational outreach, an advisory board, a sandbox program, disclosure and impact assessment requirements, and enforcement mechanisms. It applies to state agencies, local governments, and vendors contracting with state agencies for artificial intelligence deployment or use. The Act takes effect September 1, 2025.

Who it applies to

  • State agencies
  • Local governments
  • Vendors contracting with state agencies for deployment or use of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems
  • Department of Information Resources
  • Office of the Attorney General
  • Comptroller
  • Eligible entities and vendors participating in the artificial intelligence system sandbox program

Effective date

September 1, 2025 (Sec. 7)

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence system: a machine based system that for explicit or implicit objectives infers from provided information a method to generate outputs, such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions, to influence a physical or virtual environment with varying levels of autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment (Sec. 2054.003(1-a)).
  • Consequential decision: a decision that has a material legal or similarly significant effect on the provision, denial, or conditions of a person's access to a government service (Sec. 2054.003(2-b)).
  • Controlling factor: a factor that is the principal basis for making a consequential decision or capable of altering the outcome of a consequential decision (Sec. 2054.003(2-c)).
  • Heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system: an artificial intelligence system specifically intended to autonomously make, or be a controlling factor in making, a consequential decision; does not include an artificial intelligence system intended to perform a narrow procedural task, improve the result of a previously completed human activity, perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant to a consequential decision, or detect decision making patterns or deviations from previous decision making patterns (Sec. 2054.003(6-a)).
  • Principal basis: the use of an output produced by a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system to make a decision without human review, oversight, involvement, or intervention, or without meaningful consideration by a human (Sec. 2054.003(11)).
  • Unlawful harm: any condition in which the use of an artificial intelligence system results in a consequential decision that causes harm to an individual who is a member of a state or federally protected class in violation of law; does not include a developer's or deployer's offer, license, or use of a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system for the sole purpose of testing the system before deployment to identify, mitigate, or otherwise ensure compliance with state and federal law (Sec. 2054.701).
  • Eligible entity: an eligible customer under Section 2054.0525 (Sec. 2054.706(a)(1)).
  • Program: the program established by Section 2054.706 designed to allow temporary testing of an artificial intelligence system in a controlled, limited manner without requiring full compliance with otherwise applicable regulations (Sec. 2054.706(a)(2)).
  • Vendor: a person registered with the department as a contractor to provide commodity items under Section 2157.068 (Sec. 2054.706(a)(3)).

Obligations

  • The department shall collect from each state agency information on the status and condition of the agency's information technology infrastructure, including an inventory of artificial intelligence systems and heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.068(b)).

  • Local governments shall complete a review of the deployment and use of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems and, on request, provide the review to the department (Sec. 2054.0965(c)).
  • A state agency with 150 or fewer full-time employees may designate a full-time employee to serve as a data management officer or enter into an agreement with one or more state agencies to jointly employ a data management officer if approved by the department (Sec. 2054.137(a-1)).
  • The data management officer for a state agency shall annually post on the Texas Open Data Portal at least three high value data sets, excluding information that is confidential or protected from disclosure under state or federal law (Sec. 2054.137(c)).
  • The department by rule shall establish an artificial intelligence system code of ethics for use by state agencies and local governments that procure, develop, deploy, or use artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.702(a)).
  • The code of ethics must include guidance aligning with the NIST AI RMF 1.0 and addressing human oversight and control, fairness and accuracy, transparency including consumer disclosures, data privacy and security, public and internal redress including accountability and liability, and the frequency of evaluations and documentation of improvements (Sec. 2054.702(b)).
  • State agencies and local governments shall adopt the code of ethics (Sec. 2054.702(c)).
  • The department by rule shall develop minimum risk management and governance standards for the development, procurement, deployment, and use of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems by a state agency or local government (Sec. 2054.703(a)).
  • The minimum standards must be consistent with the NIST AI RMF 1.0 and include accountability measures, required assessment and documentation of known security risks, performance metrics, and transparency measures before deploying and at material changes, resources for local governments, and guidelines for risk management frameworks, acceptable use policies, employee training, and contractual vendor risk management (Sec. 2054.703(b)).
  • State agencies and local governments shall adopt the minimum standards (Sec. 2054.703(c)).
  • The department shall develop educational materials on artificial intelligence systems, training materials for state and local government employees and the general public, make training materials available on its public Internet website, and host statewide forums and training sessions (Sec. 2054.704(a)-(c)).
  • The public sector artificial intelligence systems advisory board shall obtain and disseminate information, facilitate shared resources, consult with the department, identify opportunities for state agencies to implement artificial intelligence systems and streamline procurement, and recommend elimination of rules that restrict innovation (Sec. 2054.705(b)).
  • The department shall establish and administer a sandbox program to support eligible entities in contracting with vendors for research, development, training, testing, and other predeployment activities related to artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.706(b)).
  • The department shall create an application process for vendors that includes a detailed description of the artificial intelligence system and intended use, a risk assessment addressing potential impacts on the public, and a plan for mitigating adverse consequences discovered during testing (Sec. 2054.706(c)).
  • A vendor participating in the sandbox program shall, with oversight by the department, provide eligible entities with secure access to an artificial intelligence system used in the program (Sec. 2054.706(d)).
  • The department shall provide detailed guidelines regarding the exemption from compliance with otherwise applicable regulations provided by the program (Sec. 2054.706(e)).
  • Eligible entities and vendors shall submit quarterly reports to the department including performance measures, risk mitigation strategies, feedback on program effectiveness and efficiency, and any additional information the department requests (Sec. 2054.706(f)).
  • The department shall produce an annual report and submit it to the legislature by November 30 of each even numbered year summarizing participants, outcomes, and recommendations (Sec. 2054.706(g)).
  • A state agency that procures, develops, deploys, or uses a public facing artificial intelligence system shall provide clear disclosure of interaction with the system to the public as provided by the code of ethics (Sec. 2054.707).
  • A state agency that deploys or uses a heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system or a vendor that contracts with a state agency for the deployment or use of such a system shall conduct a system assessment outlining risks of unlawful harm, system limitations, and information governance practices (Sec. 2054.708(a)).
  • The state agency or vendor shall make a copy of the assessment available to the department on request (Sec. 2054.708(b)).
  • The department shall take actions necessary to ensure the confidentiality of information submitted under the impact assessment section, including restricting access to only authorized personnel and implementing physical, electronic, and procedural protections (Sec. 2054.708(d)).
  • If a state agency or vendor becomes aware of a violation of Subchapter S, the agency or vendor shall report the violation to the department, if applicable, and the attorney general (Sec. 2054.709(a)).
  • The attorney general shall review a report or complaint and determine whether to bring an action to enjoin a violation (Sec. 2054.709(b)).
  • If the attorney general determines that a vendor violated Subchapter S, the attorney general shall provide the vendor with a written notice of the violation (Sec. 2054.709(c)).
  • If a vendor fails to respond or cure the violation within 31 days after receiving the written notice, the state agency shall provide the vendor with a notice of intent to void the contract (Sec. 2054.709(d)).
  • The attorney general shall establish a web page in collaboration with the department allowing a person to report complaints relating to artificial intelligence systems (Sec. 2054.710(a)).
  • A complaint submitted on the web page must be distributed to the department (Sec. 2054.710(b)).
  • The attorney general shall post information educating persons about risks and benefits of artificial intelligence systems and explaining a person's rights (Sec. 2054.710(d)).
  • The attorney general shall submit a report to the legislature by November 30 of each even numbered year summarizing complaints, resolutions, and enforcement actions (Sec. 2054.710(f)).
  • Each state agency and local government deploying or using an artificial intelligence system that is public facing or that is a controlling factor in a consequential decision shall include a standardized notice on all related applications, Internet websites, and public computer systems (Sec. 2054.711(a)).
  • The department shall develop a form for the standardized notice that includes general information about the system and data sources and measures taken to maintain compliance with information privacy laws and ethics standards (Sec. 2054.711(b)).
  • The department shall coordinate activities under Subchapter S and any other law relating to artificial intelligence systems to ensure efficient implementation and streamline resources (Sec. 2054.712).
  • The department shall adopt rules to implement Subchapter S (Sec. 2054.713).
  • As soon as practicable after the effective date, the Department of Information Resources shall adopt rules necessary to implement Subchapter S and develop the outreach program and form required by Sections 2054.704 and 2054.711 (Sec. 6(a)).

Prohibitions

  • The high value data sets posted by a data management officer may not include information that is confidential or protected from disclosure under state or federal law (Sec. 2054.137(c)).

  • Advisory board members are not entitled to compensation or reimbursement of expenses for service on the advisory board (Sec. 2054.705(f)).

Penalties and enforcement

The attorney general reviews reports and complaints, may bring an action to enjoin a violation, and provides written notice to vendors determined to have violated Subchapter S. If a vendor fails to cure within 31 days after written notice, the state agency provides a notice of intent to void the contract; if the vendor fails to cure within 31 days after that notice, the state agency may void the contract without further obligation.   • Health care services by an academic medical center, state owned hospital, public hospital, or hospital district organized under Article IX of the Texas Constitution or under Texas Health and Safety Code may satisfy disclosure requirements by including a generalized statement in patient consent forms that an artificial intelligence system may be used in the course of treatment (Sec. 2054.711(c)).
  • The sandbox program allows temporary testing of an artificial intelligence system in a controlled, limited manner without requiring full compliance with otherwise applicable regulations (Sec. 2054.706(a)(2), (e)).
  • Impact assessments are confidential and not subject to disclosure under Chapter 552; the state agency or department may redact or withhold information as confidential without requesting a decision from the attorney general (Sec. 2054.708(c)).
  • The department may operate the sandbox program as a statewide technology center under Subchapter L notwithstanding Section 2054.383 (Sec. 2054.706(h)).
  • The department may share information and resources for the sandbox program with any other department program established to allow a person to test an artificial intelligence system for a limited time and on a limited basis without holding a license or certificate of registration (Sec. 2054.706(i)).
  • The department may use money appropriated to the department to produce educational materials and may contract with a vendor to produce those materials (Sec. 2054.704(d)).
  • A state agency with 150 or fewer full-time employees may designate a full-time employee as a data management officer or enter into an agreement with one or more state agencies to jointly employ a data management officer if approved by the department (Sec. 2054.137(a-1)).

Compliance steps

  • Identify whether any artificial intelligence systems are heightened scrutiny, public facing, or controlling factors in consequential decisions (Sec. 2054.003, Sec. 2054.707, Sec. 2054.711).
  • Inventory all artificial intelligence systems and heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems in information technology infrastructure reports and information resources reviews (Sec. 2054.068(b), Sec. 2054.0965(b)(6)).
  • Adopt the department's artificial intelligence code of ethics and minimum risk management standards once rules are adopted (Sec. 2054.702(c), Sec. 2054.703(c)).
  • For public facing artificial intelligence systems, provide clear disclosure of interaction unless a reasonable person would know (Sec. 2054.707).
  • For public facing or controlling factor artificial intelligence systems, include the department's standardized notice on all related applications, Internet websites, and public computer systems (Sec. 2054.711(a)-(b)).
  • For heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence systems, conduct a system assessment outlining risks of unlawful harm, system limitations, and information governance practices, and make it available to the department on request while keeping it confidential (Sec. 2054.708).
  • If a vendor, implement risk management frameworks as contractually required, participate in the sandbox program if applicable, and submit quarterly reports (Sec. 2054.703(b)(4)(B), Sec. 2054.706).
  • Report any known violation of Subchapter S to the department and attorney general; respond to written notices and cure violations within 31 days to avoid contract voiding (Sec. 2054.709).
  • Local governments complete a review of heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence deployment and provide it to the department on request (Sec. 2054.0965(c)).
  • For state agencies, designate or jointly employ a data management officer if 150 or fewer employees, and ensure the data management officer posts high value data sets excluding confidential information (Sec. 2054.137).
  • Monitor department rules, code of ethics, minimum standards, educational materials, and the attorney general's complaint web page; comply with enforcement actions (Sec. 2054.702, Sec. 2054.703, Sec. 2054.704, Sec. 2054.710, Sec. 2054.713).

 SUBCHAPTER S. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 
 
 
 
  
 
         Sec.   2054.701.     DEFINITION. In this subchapter, "unlawful

 developer's or deployer's offer, license, or use of a heightened 
 
 
 
  
 
 scrutiny artificial intelligence system for the sole purpose of

         Sec.   2054.702.     ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM CODE OF

 intelligence system code of ethics for use by state agencies and 
 
 
 
  
 
 local governments that procure, develop, deploy, or use artificial 
 
 
 
  
 
 intelligence systems.

               (6)     the frequency of evaluations and documentation of

 scrutiny artificial intelligence systems by a state agency or local 
 
 
 
  
 
 government.
